messages.subject: Re: runCrossValidate memory limitation?
parts:
Hi Chris,

We haven't spent a lot of time fine-tuning `runCrossValidate`, so it's perhaps not too surprising you're running into some bumps. 
Coincidentally, in another recent post, we had a discussion of clearing compiled objects to release memory.
To use those strategies, you'd have to modify `nimble:::calcCrossVal`, which is called by `runCrossValidate` and carries out an individual MCMC run.
Ideally we'd add an argument to `runCrossValidate` so that the compiled objects can be cleared based on that.

As far as the dynamic index out of bounds, nothing obvious is coming to mind as to why that would happen in some of the MCMCs. 
You might check the initial values for `x[1:N,1]` or for `morpho_prob[1:M]` (for example you could use R's debugging tools
and/or modify `nimble:::calcCrossVal` to be able to check on values for individual chains) and/or trying running one of the hold-out MCMCs "manually"
outside of `runCrossValidate`.

-chris


On Mon, Feb 20, 2023 at 12:59 AM Chris Carleton <w.cca...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi All,

I'm trying to run a leave-one-out CV using runCrossValidate (script attached, see line 137 for the call to runCrossValidate), but the R session keeps crashing/getting killed. I think it's a memory issue because I can see that system memory usage going up as the cross validation runs. If I run just a few folds (say k <50) the memory usage grows but the process doesn't get killed---I assume because it doesn't go over the limit. When I try run the leave-one-out, though, I get less than half way through (169 observations) before all ~32 G of memory are consumed and the process gets shut down. Is this just a limitation of using the provided runCrossValidate() given that the model has to be recompiled each iteration? Is there someway to get R to release the memory?

Also, for some reason I'm getting a dynamic index out of bounds warning while running runCrossValidate that doesn't come up when I just run the model on it's own with nimbleMCMC() (see line 120). Any ideas about that would be appreciated, too!

Many thanks,
Chris
